object_description: three linked buildings organized around an entrance square and recreation area
design_condition: Three buildings are linked along Billeweg to form an entrance square and recreation area, while the pavilion-like basic-level wing opens toward the park and natural ground.

positive.statement: The common center is functionally well designed, with the assembly hall, kitchen, library and day school clearly organized.

position.rationale: Central linked zone is approximated between the three visible building masses.

positive.statement: The division into three structures creates controlled intermediate spaces and the desired external layout without the complex falling apart.

position.rationale: Top and elevation views clearly show three separated, linked volumes.

positive.statement: The pavilion-like basic level responds well to its use and allows permeability from the residential buildings to the park.

position.rationale: Low elongated pavilion mass is visibly distinct from the taller residential volumes.

positive.statement: The outdoor sports facilities are fulfilled according to the space allocation plan and are well arranged.

position.rationale: Open recreation area is estimated beside the linked masses in the top view.

positive.statement: The room program for changing rooms, equipment rooms and material rooms is complete and well organized.

position.target: changing rooms, equipment rooms and material rooms
position.rationale: Support rooms are not distinguishable, so they are anchored near the lower building edge.

positive.statement: The various buildings have a clean structural solution, and the gymnasium ceiling uses an interesting truss construction.

position.rationale: Ceiling height is constrained within the taller hall volume, though truss members are unresolved.

negative.statement: The elementary-school location is not entirely unproblematic in urban-planning terms.

position.rationale: School placement is approximated across the building-and-open-space composition.

negative.statement: The roof gardens are too limited to work convincingly as break areas in the proposed arrangement.

position.rationale: Upper surfaces of the taller right-hand mass provide the likely roof-garden location.

negative.statement: The allocation of group rooms is unfavorable, and one break area would serve four classrooms.

position.rationale: Interior group rooms are absent, anchored approximately within the central school mass.

negative.statement: The escape-route concept was not considered feasible and requires revision.

position.rationale: Circulation system is not represented, placed approximately through the linked building network.

negative.statement: The proposed façades are too vaguely formulated and leave too much room for interpretation.

position.rationale: Exterior envelopes are visible, with the south-facing frontage used as representative evidence.

negative.statement: The buried gymnasium provides little stimulation and social control of the above-ground pitches.

position.rationale: Low hall-like mass is estimated beneath or beside the visible pitches.

negative.statement: The classroom access and outdoor-space arrangement forms a problematic knot that can hardly be solved.

position.rationale: The spatial knot is approximated at the central transition between buildings and open areas.

negative.statement: The daycare-center rooms lack clear allocation to care groups, and some room functions remain unclear.

position.rationale: Interior daycare allocation is not visible, anchored within the low pavilion volume.

negative.statement: The project is costly in terms of maintenance and building cleaning.

position.rationale: Operational cost judgment has no useful spatial referent.
